'''''Wallisia cyanea''''', or '''pink quill''', is a [[species]] of plant of the genus ''[[Wallisia]]'' in the [[bromeliad family]], native to the rainforests of Ecuador. An [[epiphyte|epiphytic]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] growing to {{convert|50|cm|0|abbr=on}} high by {{convert|50|cm|0|abbr=on}} wide, it has stemless rosettes of thin, recurved leaves and paddle-shaped spikes of 20 pink bracts with violet flowers, in spring and autumn.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>

The Latin [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] ''cyanea'' means "blue", referring to the intense purple-violet hue of the flowers.<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book|last=Harrison|first=Lorraine|title=RHS Latin for gardeners|year=2012|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=9781845337315|pages=224}}</ref>

With a minimum temperature of {{convert|7|C|F|abbr=on}}, this plant is often cultivated as a low-maintenance [[houseplant]] in [[temperateness|temperate]] regions, often sold alongside orchids or by itself.<ref name=RHSAZ /> It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Tillandsia cyanea''|url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=3513|accessdate=27 June 2013}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

''Wallisia cyanea'' was formerly placed in ''[[Tillandsia]]'', but following [[DNA analysis]], was reassigned to ''Wallisia''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bromeliad.org.au/news/DD0217.htm|title=Bromeliads in Australia - DNA / New genera|website=www.bromeliad.org.au|access-date=2019-06-15}}</ref>

Cultivars of ''W. cyanea'' include ''Wallisia'' 'Anita' and ''Wallisia'' 'Sandy'.<ref>[http://www.bsi.org/bcr/Tillandsia/Anita.html BSI BCR Entry for 'Anita']</ref><ref>[http://www.bsi.org/bcr/Tillandsia/Sandy.html BSI BCR Entry for 'Sandy']</ref>
